ASSIGNMENT AND ASSUMPTION OF LEASE AND CONSENT OF LANDLORD

THIS ASSIGNMENT AND ASSUMPTION OF LEASE (this "Assignment") is made as of December 15, 2026, among ROWANWOOD DESIGN STUDIO LLC, a New York limited liability company ("Assignor"), MERIDIAN TYPEWORKS INC., a Delaware corporation ("Assignee"), and GRANDVIEW HOLDINGS 447 LLC, a New York limited liability company ("Landlord").

RECITALS

A. Landlord, as landlord, and Assignor, as tenant, are parties to a Lease dated April 1, 2023, as amended by a First Amendment dated September 8, 2024 (as amended, the "Lease"), covering approximately 6,200 rentable square feet on the fourth floor of the building at 447 Grandview Avenue, Brooklyn, New York (the "Premises").

B. Assignor wishes to assign its entire interest in the Lease to Assignee, Assignee wishes to assume it, and Landlord is willing to consent on the terms below.

NOW, THEREFORE, the parties agree as follows.

1. Assignment.

Effective as of January 1, 2027 (the "Effective Date"), Assignor assigns, transfers, and conveys to Assignee all of Assignor's right, title, and interest in, to, and under the Lease, together with the security deposit held by Landlord in the amount of $37,200 and all rights to it.

2. Assumption.

As of the Effective Date, Assignee assumes and agrees to perform and be bound by every obligation of the tenant under the Lease arising on and after the Effective Date, as if Assignee had been the original tenant, and agrees to be liable directly to Landlord for that performance.

3. Assignor's Continuing Liability.

Assignor is not released from its obligations under the Lease. Assignor remains liable to Landlord for the full performance of the tenant's obligations for the balance of the Term, including any renewal or extension and any obligation arising from a subsequent amendment to which Assignor is not a party, except that Assignor is not liable for an increase in the tenant's monetary obligations that results from an amendment made without Assignor's written consent. Landlord may proceed against Assignor without first proceeding against Assignee, and Assignor waives any requirement of notice of default given to Assignee.

4. Landlord's Consent.

Landlord consents to this Assignment. That consent is limited to this Assignment and is not a consent to any further assignment, sublease, or other transfer, each of which continues to require Landlord's prior written consent under Article 11 of the Lease. Landlord's consent is not a waiver of any provision of the Lease and is not an acknowledgment that the Lease is free of default.

5. Estoppel Statements by Landlord.

Landlord states that, as of the date of this Assignment and to Landlord's actual knowledge: (a) the Lease is in full force and effect and has not been amended except by the First Amendment; (b) base rent is currently $24,800 per month and has been paid through December 31, 2026; (c) Landlord holds a security deposit of $37,200; and (d) no notice of default has been given to Assignor that remains uncured.

6. Assignor's Representations.

Assignor represents that it is the sole tenant under the Lease, that it has not previously assigned, sublet, mortgaged, or encumbered its interest, that to its knowledge no default by Landlord or by Assignor exists, and that it has delivered to Assignee a true and complete copy of the Lease and the First Amendment.

7. Indemnity.

Assignor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Assignee from and against any claim, loss, liability, or expense, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising from the tenant's obligations under the Lease attributable to the period before the Effective Date. Assignee shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Assignor from and against the same, attributable to the period on and after the Effective Date. The party seeking indemnity shall give prompt written notice, shall permit the indemnifying party to control the defense with counsel reasonably satisfactory to it, and shall not settle without the indemnifying party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

8. Broker.

Each of Assignor and Assignee represents that it dealt with no broker in connection with this Assignment other than Halverson Retail Advisors, whose commission Assignor shall pay under a separate agreement, and each shall indemnify the others against any claim by a broker with whom it dealt.

9. Condition of the Premises.

Assignee accepts the Premises in their "as is, where is" condition as of the Effective Date, with no representation by Landlord or Assignor as to fitness, and Landlord has no obligation to perform any work or to provide any allowance in connection with this Assignment.

10. Notices; Governing Law; Counterparts.

Every notice under this Assignment shall be given in the manner Article 24 of the Lease requires, to the addresses stated below each party's signature. This Assignment is governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles, and each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Kings County, New York. This Assignment may be executed in counterparts and may be amended only by a writing signed by all three parties.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Assignment as of the date first written above.
